s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute neurological decline with mass effect and subsequent respiratory decompensation
salient_findings: Ring-enhancing lesion in the right temporal lobe
Positive toxoplasma IgG and DNA-PCR for Toxoplasma gondii in CSF
New left upper lobe opacification with diffuse reticulonodular interstitial prominence on chest radiograph
key_facts: 1½-week history of headache and blurred vision
MRI showed a 2.7-cm ring-enhancing lesion in the right temporal lobe with mass effect
HIV infection with a CD4 count <20 cells/µL
HIV viral load of 191 000 copies/mL
Elevated serum toxoplasma IgG
CSF studies showed 48 cells/µL (97% lymphocytes)
Positive toxoplasma IgG and DNA-PCR for Toxoplasma gondii in CSF
Histopathologic examination of the brain tissue revealed bradyzoites and tachyzoites
Fever to 39.6 °C
Generalized weakness
1-day history of productive cough
Chest radiograph showed a new left upper lobe opacification
CT scan of the chest confirmed extensive reticulonodular interstitial infiltrates

shortlist.label: Toxoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Positive toxoplasma IgG and DNA-PCR for Toxoplasma gondii in CSF, histopathologic examination of the brain tissue revealed bradyzoites and tachyzoites

shortlist.label: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: HIV infection with a CD4 count <20 cells/µL, respiratory symptoms and radiographic findings consistent with opportunistic infection

shortlist.label: Primary central nervous system lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Subacute neurological decline with mass effect, HIV infection increasing risk for lymphoma

shortlist.label: Cytomegalovirus encephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: HIV infection with a low CD4 count, neurological symptoms and potential for CMV reactivation

shortlist.label: Cerebral cryptococcosis
shortlist.why_kept: HIV infection with a CD4 count <20 cells/µL, initial presentation with neurological symptoms and mass effect

shortlist.label: Invasive aspergillosis
shortlist.why_kept: HIV infection with a low CD4 count, respiratory symptoms and radiographic findings consistent with opportunistic infection

shortlist.label: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy
shortlist.why_kept: HIV infection with a low CD4 count, subacute neurological decline

shortlist.label: Cytomegalovirus pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: HIV infection with a low CD4 count, respiratory symptoms and radiographic findings consistent with opportunistic infection

raw.rationale: The patient's MRI showed a ring-enhancing lesion, and CSF studies were positive for toxoplasma IgG and DNA-PCR for Toxoplasma gondii, with histopathologic examination revealing bradyzoites and tachyzoites, all of which are consistent with toxoplasmosis, particularly in the context of the patient's severely immunocompromised state due to HIV infection with a very low CD4 count.

rejected.label: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia
rejected.why: While the patient's immunocompromised state puts him at risk for Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia, the initial presentation and diagnostic findings were more indicative of toxoplasmosis, and there was no specific evidence provided for Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia in the initial diagnosis.

rejected.label: Primary central nervous system lymphoma
rejected.why: The histopathologic examination revealed bradyzoites and tachyzoites, which are indicative of toxoplasmosis, not lymphoma.

rejected.label: Cytomegalovirus encephalitis
rejected.why: There is no mention of CMV detection in the CSF or brain tissue, making this diagnosis less likely than toxoplasmosis based on the provided information.

rejected.label: Cerebral cryptococcosis
rejected.why: CSF studies were negative for cryptococcal antigen, which makes this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Invasive aspergillosis
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence provided for invasive aspergillosis in the initial diagnosis or the follow-up presentation.

rejected.label: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy
rejected.why: This condition is associated with JC virus infection and typically presents with different clinical and radiological findings than those described for this patient.

rejected.label: Cytomegalovirus pneumonia
rejected.why: While the patient developed respiratory symptoms, the initial diagnosis and treatment focused on toxoplasmosis, and there's no direct evidence provided for CMV pneumonia in the information given.

rejected.label: Primary central nervous system lymphoma
rejected.why: The presence of toxoplasma IgG and DNA-PCR for Toxoplasma gondii in CSF, along with the histopathologic findings, strongly supports toxoplasmosis over lymphoma.
